text:
The week's headlines share a theme. Squawka: "The Goal Scorer Is Passing Now." The Leafs Nation: "career-best playmaking." Auston Matthews has 15 assists to go with 11 goals, 26 points in 17 games, and a five-game point streak. By our wins-added count, which weighs goals by how much they swung the game, he ranks 2nd of 496 skaters.

Some of it is real. Toronto takes 54.9% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 14.9 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 99th-percentile competition last season with teammates in the bottom 6%.

Some of it isn't. He's shooting 21.6% against a range centred on 13.8%, and the Leafs have scored 9.1 more goals than their chances with him on the ice. His 4.46 points per 60 sits well above the top of our range (3.35). The projection still lands at 76 to 104 points, a long way from last season's 53 in 60 games.

One thing to watch: his ice time is down more than two minutes a night over the last ten. With John Tavares nearing a return, the minutes may shift again.
headline: Matthews is passing now, and the bounces help
